sources.articleTitle: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri over unsafe packaged drinking water
Bisleri Under Scanner After Carcinogenic Substances Found In Water Sample
FSSAI orders prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water

headline: FSSAI Initiates Prosecution Against Bisleri Over Unsafe Water Samples
metaDescription: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has ordered legal action against Bisleri International after water samples failed regulatory safety tests.
aiSummaryBullets: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has initiated prosecution proceedings against Bisleri International.
Regulators stated that analyzed water samples failed to meet mandatory safety thresholds for bromate content.
The product was declared unsafe for consumption based on the standards outlined in the Food Safety and Standards Act of 2006.
aiContextParagraph: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has taken formal action against Bisleri International following reports that their packaged drinking water products were found to be non-compliant with federal safety standards. According to the regulator, testing revealed that the water samples contained levels of bromate exceeding the prescribed legal limits. Under the mandates established by the Food Safety and Standards Act of 2006, the agency has classified the affected samples as unsafe for human consumption. This development has prompted the FSSAI to sanction legal prosecution against the company. These regulatory findings focus on chemical safety benchmarks enforced by the agency to ensure public health compliance within the packaged beverage industry. Bisleri International is now subject to legal proceedings as authorities address the identified safety violations related to their water quality analysis and regulatory adherence.
whyItIsViral: The story is trending due to significant public search interest in the brand name and reports across multiple major news outlets following the regulatory announcement.
